column3: The word for "I" and "me": Chinese does not change the pronoun between subject and object, so 我 is the same in 我看他 and 他看我. 我 began as a picture of a weapon with three blades and was only borrowed for its sound to write "I", so the shape carries no meaning of "I".
Singular "you". The 亻 (person) gives the meaning and 尔 gives the sound; the same 亻 starts 他, 们 and 住. For more than one person add 们: 你们. For someone you want to treat with respect there is 您.
He or "him". The 亻 (person) gives the meaning and 也 gives the sound. 他 and 她 are both said tā, so in speech only the context tells you which is meant; only the writing differs.
She or "her". It is 女 (woman) next to the same 也 that is in 他, so the two characters differ only on the left. Said tā, exactly like 他.
A polite "you" for one person, used to show respect: 您好, 请问您贵姓. It is 你 written above 心 (heart), which fits its respectful tone. Use it for a single person only; for a group say 你们.

Added after 我, 你, 他 or a word for people to make a plural: 我们, 孩子们. Do not use it together with a number: 三个孩子, not 三个孩子们. 亻 (people) gives the meaning and 门 (mén) gives the sound; in traditional 們 the sound part is 門. It is read men, with no tone.
We or "us": 我 plus the plural ending 们, which is light, so it is read wǒmen. Put 的 after it to say "our": 我们的老师.
You for two or more people: 你 plus 们. It works as subject, object and, with 的, as "your": 你们的老师. For one person use 你, or 您 to be polite.
They for a group of men, or a group of men and women together. If everyone in the group is female, 她们 is used instead. Both are said tāmen.
They for a group made up only of women or girls; for a mixed group the writing uses 他们. Said exactly like 他们, so it is a distinction of the written language.

Good or "well", and on its own the answer "OK, fine". It is 女 (woman) and 子 (child); the usual explanation is that a woman with a child was seen as good. Read hǎo here; as "to like" it is read hào, as in 爱好.
column7: The weather is very nice today.

column3: Thank you. The word 谢 is said twice and the second is light: xièxie. The usual reply is 不客气. In 谢, 讠 (speech) gives the meaning and 射 the sound; traditional 謝 has 言 for speech.
The usual reply to 谢谢: "you're welcome". It is 不 plus 客气 ("to stand on ceremony, be polite"), so it means "no need to be formal". In 客 (guest), 宀 (roof) sits over 各, which gives the sound.
Sorry, for a mistake or for bumping into someone. Literally "cannot face (you)": 对 is "face, towards" and 不起 "cannot manage to". The usual answer is 没关系.
It doesn't matter: the answer to 对不起. Literally "no connection": 没 (not have) plus 关系 (relationship). In traditional 關 the gate 門 is visible; the simplified 关 drops the gate.
It's nothing, said after thanks or an apology to wave it away. Literally "not have anything": 没 plus 什么 (what, here "anything"). It can also mean "nothing in particular".
Goodbye, literally "again see". The 见 alone means "see"; its traditional form 見 is an eye 目 on top of a person (a kneeling figure with a large eye for a head).

Please: put it before a verb to ask politely, as in 请坐. It also means "to invite" or "to treat": 我请你吃饭 is "my treat". 讠 (speech) gives the meaning and 青 the sound (qīng, close to qǐng); traditional 請 has 言.
Excuse me, may I ask: said before a question to someone you do not know. Literally "please ask". In 问, 口 (mouth) gives the meaning and 门 (mén) gives the sound, close to wèn.
column7: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

column3: Please come in, said to someone at the door. The 辶 in 进 (walk) is the meaning part; where the simplified 进 has 井 (jǐng), the traditional 進 has 隹 (a bird).
column7: Please come in and sit down.

column3: Please sit down, what a host says to a guest. 坐 has 土 (earth, ground) at the bottom. After 坐 you can add the place: 请坐这里.
One: an ideogram, a single horizontal stroke. 二 and 三 add strokes. The tone changes in speech (yí before a fourth tone, yì before the others: 一个 yí gè, 一天 yì tiān) but dictionaries write yī.
Two: two parallel strokes. Use 二 for counting and in numbers (二十, 第二, 二月), but 两 before a measure word: 两个人, not 二个人.
column6: Jīntiān shì èr yuè èr hào.

column3: Three: three parallel strokes. A number goes in front of a measure word: 三个人, 三本书. 三 is also the base of 星期三 (Wednesday).
Four. 四 began as a picture of a nose breathing out and was borrowed for the number because of its sound; older writing used four stacked strokes, which was too easy to mix up with 二 and 三.
Five. There are several theories (a tally mark, the palm lines of a hand) and none is settled, so treat it as a shape to memorize. 五 is also the base of 星期五 (Friday).
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
column7: There are five people in my family.

column3: Six. Two ideas are offered, a picture of a shed or an old counting symbol, and neither is certain. 星期六 is Saturday.
Seven. It is a horizontal and a vertical stroke crossing, originally the character for 切 "to cut". Unlike 十, the vertical stroke of 七 ends in a bend (乚).
Eight. It is two bent lines meaning "to divide", later borrowed for the number because of the sound. The idea of dividing is still visible in 半 and 分, which both contain 八.
Nine. It is a picture of an arm bent at the elbow (the hook at the lower right is the bend); the word for "elbow" is now written 肘.
Ten: a crossing of a horizontal and a vertical stroke; early forms were a single vertical stroke and the origin is debated. 11-19 are 十 plus a digit (十一), 20-90 a digit plus 十 (二十).
Zero, and the word for a gap in the middle of a number: 105 is 一百零五. 雨 (rain) gives the meaning and 令 the sound, which is líng in both.
column6: Zhè běn shū yībǎi líng wǔ kuài.

column3: A circle used as a written zero. It is how years and phone numbers are read digit by digit: 二〇〇〇年 is èr líng líng líng nián. 零 is the same sound and is used in counting, as in 一百零五.
column6: Wǒ èr líng líng líng nián chūshēng.

column3: Two before a measure word: 两个人, 两本书; use 二 for counting and in numbers. It also means "a couple of": 过两天 is "in a couple of days".
Hundred: 一 on top of 白. 白 is the sound part (bǎi against bái). You must keep the 一 for 100: say 一百, not just 百.
column7: This cup is a hundred yuan.

column3: How many, asked about a small number (about ten or fewer): 几个人? The simplified 几 is a picture of a small table seen from the side; the traditional 幾 is built differently. For larger or open quantities use 多少.
column7: How many friends do you have?

column3: How many or "how much", for any size of quantity. Literally "many-few". The second syllable is light: duōshao. The standard question for prices is 多少钱？
Half. 八 (divide) over 牛 (ox): it is read as cutting an ox in two. In 半个小时 the 半 comes before the measure word, but "an hour and a half" is 一个半小时. 三点半 is half past three.
Put before a number to make an ordinal: 第一, 第二个. ⺮ (bamboo) on top is the meaning part, standing for the bamboo strips used to write on, and 弟 gives the sound; both are read dì.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ dìyī cì lái.
column7: This is my first time here.

column3: Person. It is a side view of a standing person. At the left of other characters it shrinks to 亻 (你, 他, 住, 休). Add it to a country to name its people: 中国人.
column7: There are a lot of people here.

column3: Male. 田 (field) over 力 (strength): it is read as the person who supplies the strength to work a field. It pairs with 女, and starts 男人, 男生 and 男朋友.
Female. It is a picture of a woman with folded arms, kneeling or standing. As the left part of other characters it marks women and female relatives: 妈, 姐, 妹, 奶, 好. Pinyin is nǚ (typed nv).
column6: Tā shì yī wèi nǚ yīshēng.

column3: Mom, as a form of address (妈！) or with a possessive (我妈). 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 马 (mǎ) gives the sound, close to mā. The traditional 媽 has 馬 as its sound part.
Mom. Family terms are often doubled (爸爸, 哥哥, 姐姐, 弟弟, 妹妹), and the second syllable is light: māma. Chinese says 爸爸妈妈, with father first.
Dad, as a form of address (爸！) or with a possessive (我爸). 父 (father) on top gives the meaning and 巴 (bā) gives the sound, close to bà. The same 巴 is in 吧.
Dad, with a light second syllable: bàba. 爸 is a colloquial form of 父 (father), which is why it is built from 父 plus a sound part.
Older brother. It is two 可 stacked; the character first meant "to sing, song" and the sense "older brother" is a later borrowing. The "song" meaning survives in 歌, which has 哥 as its sound part.
column6: Wǒ gē bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
column7: My older brother is three years older than me.

column3: Older brother, with a light second syllable: gēge. Chinese always says whether a sibling is older or younger: 哥哥 and 姐姐 are older, 弟弟 and 妹妹 are younger.
column7: My older brother works in Beijing.

column3: Older sister. 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 且 the sound, though qiě and jiě are only loosely alike. Alone it turns up in 小姐 and as an address after a name; the everyday word is 姐姐.
column7: My older sister is a teacher.

column3: Older sister, with a light second syllable: jiějie. It is also what you may call a young woman a little older than you who is not a relative.
column7: My older sister is taller than me.

column3: Younger brother. It is a picture of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping suggested order or sequence, which stretched to "the one after", a younger brother. 第 (the ordinal marker) is 弟 with ⺮ on top and sounds the same, dì.
column7: My younger brother is at school.

column3: Younger brother, with a light second syllable: dìdi. It is also what you may call a boy a bit younger than you. In the pair 哥哥 / 弟弟 Chinese always says older or younger.
column6: Dìdi bǐ wǒ xiǎo liǎng suì.
column7: My younger brother is two years younger than me.

column3: Younger sister. 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 未 gives the sound (wèi against mèi). Alone it appears in forms like 我妹 and 妹妹, which is the everyday word.
column7: My younger sister is ten this year.

column3: Younger sister, with a light second syllable: mèimei. The 女 on the left marks the female relative and 未 is the sound part, as in 妹.
Grandmother on the father's side (the father's mother). 奶 has 女 (woman) as meaning part and 乃 as sound part (both nǎi); by itself 奶 means "milk", as in 牛奶.
column7: My grandmother is seventy this year.

column3: Grandfather on the father's side. The 父 (father) on top is the meaning part; the traditional 爺 has 耶 (yé) as its sound part, which the simplified 爷 shortens to 卩. The second 爷 is light: yéye.
column7: Grandpa is watching TV at home.

column3: Son. 儿 is the simplified form of 兒, a picture of a child (an infant with a soft skull), and 子 also means "child", so it is "child-child". 子 is light: érzi. Here 儿 is a full syllable, not the ending of words like 这儿.
Daughter: 女 (female) plus 儿 (child). In pinyin an apostrophe splits the syllables so they do not run together: nǚ'ér.
Child, kid, also "one's children": 你有孩子吗？ 孩 has 子 (child) as meaning part and 亥 as sound part (hài, close to hái). The final 子 is light.

A light ending that makes many nouns: 桌子, 房子, 杯子, 孩子. It has no meaning of its own there. Read zǐ it means "child; son". The shape is a baby with a big head, spread arms and legs wrapped in a blanket.
Family members: 家 (home) plus 人 (people). 一家人 is "a family, all of one household". In 家, 宀 (roof) sits over what is now written 豕 (pig), though that bottom part was originally a sound part.
This. Before a noun it normally needs a measure word: 这个人, 这本书. In speech it is often said zhèi, especially before a measure word. The traditional form is 這; 辶 (walk) is the part on the left.

That. The 阝 on the right is the "city" part, because the character was first the name of a state; it was later borrowed for "that". 这 is near, 那 is far. Read nà; the question word 哪 (nǎ) is 那 with 口 added.
Here, said zhèr: the spoken ending 儿 fuses with zhè and has no tone of its own. It means the same as 这里.
There, said nàr. The opposite of 这儿. Use it with 在 for locations: 我的书在那儿. Do not confuse with 哪儿 (nǎr, "where"), which has 口 added and a different tone.
Here. It means the same as 这儿. The 里 (inside) is written 裡 in traditional characters (衤 for clothing, with 里 giving the sound), so the word is 這裡. Heard as zhèli.
There, the same meaning as 那儿. Traditional 那裡 (some print 那裏); 里 is the "inside" character, light in speech. In this word 里 does not mean "inside", it just makes a place word.
column7: There is a shop over there.

column3: These. 些 means "some, several" and is already a plural measure, so the noun follows directly: 这些书, with no 个. Used alone it also works as a pronoun: 这些是我的.
column6: Zhèxiē shū dōu shì xīn de.

column3: Those: 那 plus 些, a plural measure, so no 个 before the noun: 那些人. It can also stand alone as a pronoun: 那些是我的衣服.
This side, over here: 这边请 is "this way, please". 边 means "side": 辶 (walk) is its meaning part. The traditional 邊 has 臱 as sound part where the simplified 边 has 力.
That side, over there. The 边 is light: nàbian. Often used to point things out against 这边: 这边是学校，那边是商店.
column7: There is a station over there.

column3: What. The question word stays where the answer would go: 你吃什么？ ("you eat what?"). Before a noun it asks "what kind": 什么书？ Traditional is 什麼; the simplified 么 is a variant of 幺.
column7: What do you want to eat?

column3: Who. It is read shéi in speech; shuí is another reading. 讠 (speech) is the meaning part; the traditional 誰 uses 言 and keeps 隹 on the right as sound part.

Which: put it before a measure word, 哪个, 哪本书. It is 那 (nà) with 口 (mouth) added, so the two look alike and differ in sound only by tone, nǎ against nà. Only the 口 tells a question from a pointing word.
Where, said nǎr. Ask for a place with 你去哪儿？ or 你在哪儿？ Compare 那儿 (nàr, "there"), which is the same without the 口.
Where, the same meaning as 哪儿. Traditional 哪裡. Said twice, 哪里哪里, it is a modest reply to a compliment, "not at all".
Which ones (plural), for choosing among several things: 哪些书？ The noun follows directly, without 个. For a single thing say 哪个.
How or "why": 去机场怎么走？ asks how to go; 你怎么了？ asks what is wrong. 心 (heart) is the meaning part of 怎, and 乍 the sound. Before the verb it asks about way, not reason.
column7: How do I get to the airport?

column3: What are you doing? or "what for?", a spoken phrase: 你在干什么？ This 干 is gàn ("do"), written 幹 in traditional; the other 干 (gān, "dry") is written 乾.
A question that expects "yes": 你是不是累了？ It is 是 + 不 + 是, the "verb, not, verb" way of asking. The middle 不 is light: shìbushì. Add it to the end of a statement to check it: 他是老师，是不是？
To be. It links two nouns: 我是学生. It is not used before an adjective: say 我很高兴, not 我是高兴. The origin is unclear, so there is nothing to read from the shape.
To have and "there is": 我有一本书; 桌子上有一本书. Its negative is 没有, never 不有. On top is a hand 又 (yòu), which gives the sound, and the 月 below is a changed 肉 "meat".
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
column7: There are four people in my family.

column3: At, in, be located: 我在家. Before a verb it gives the place of the action (我在学校学习) or marks an action in progress (他在吃饭).
Not, no. Put it before verbs and adjectives: 不好. Before another fourth tone it is said bú (不是 is bú shì), but dictionaries write bù. It is a picture of a flower's calyx, borrowed for the word "not".
Not (have): negates 有 and past actions: 我没吃, 我没有书. Never use 不 for past actions. 氵 (water) is the left part of both 没 and the traditional 沒.
Does not have, "there is no", and the negative of past actions: 他没有来 ("he did not come"). At the end of a question it asks "did you or not": 你吃了没有？
column7: I don't have an older brother.

column3: Correct, right: 你说得对. Also "toward, to": 他对我很好 ("he is good to me"). The simplified 对 is a hand 又 plus 寸; the traditional 對 is built differently.
column6: Zhè ge zì duì bu duì?

column3: Wrong, mistaken, the opposite of 对: 写错了. 钅 (metal) is the meaning part and 昔 the sound (xī); traditional 錯 has 釒. It follows a verb to say how it went: 说错, 写错.
Not right, wrong: 这个字不对. Also said to stop someone: 不对！ ("wait, that's wrong"). Before a fourth tone 不 is said bú: bú duì.
Not big: 房间不大. In speech it can also mean "not very": 不大好 "not very good". 大 is the opposite of 小.
No need to: 不用谢 ("no need to thank me"), 不用去 ("you don't have to go"). It is 不 plus 用 ("use"); the answer to an offer of help can be 不用，谢谢.
Also, too. It goes after the subject, before the verb: 我也是学生. With 都 the order is 也都: 他们也都是学生. There are several unrelated theories for the shape, so treat it as a shape to memorize.
All, both: it comes after the group it covers and before the verb: 我们都是学生. 阝 on the right is the meaning part ("city") and 者 the sound. Read dū it means "capital city".
Very. With an adjective it is almost required in a plain statement: 她很高; just 她高 sounds like a comparison. Then 很 is often weak, close to "is". 彳 (step) is the meaning part and 艮 the sound.
Too, excessively: 太贵了. Usually with 了 at the end; 太好了！ means "great!". 太 was made from 大 by adding a dot, so the two are easy to mix up when writing: 大 has no dot.
Extremely, used like 很 before adjectives: 非常好. Literally "not ordinary": 非 ("not") plus 常 ("ordinary"). 非 is two wings pointing opposite ways, later borrowed for "not".
Really, truly: 真好吃. Put it before an adjective for emphasis. Older forms of 真 (a spoon and a tripod vessel) differ from the modern shape, so its present parts are no guide to the meaning.
column6: Zhè ge zì zhēn nán xiě.
column7: This character is really hard to write.

column3: Really, truly: as a question, 真的吗？ "really?"; as a statement, 我真的不知道. After a noun, 的 gives "real, genuine": 真的钱.
OK, will do, as an answer: 行，没问题. Also "allowed": 这样行吗？ Its opposite is 不行. It is a picture of a street crossing, split into 彳 and 亍. In 银行 (bank) it is read háng.
column7: Is it OK to go today?

column3: Friend. Both characters are made of a pair: 朋 is two 月, which were once strings of cowrie shells, not moons, and 友 is two hands 又, read as friendship. The last syllable is light: péngyou.
column6: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.

column3: Boyfriend. It is a fixed word: 男 ("male") plus 朋友 does not simply mean a friend who is male. Say 我男朋友 or 我的男朋友.
Girlfriend, the partner of 男朋友. It is a fixed word and does not just mean a friend who is a woman. Without 的 it is natural: 我女朋友.
column6: Tā de nǚ péngyou shì lǎoshī.

column3: Literally "little friend": a friendly word for a child, used by teachers and adults: 小朋友，你几岁了？ Plural 小朋友们 for a group. The last syllable is third tone here: xiǎopéngyǒu.
column7: Little one, how old are you?

column3: Boy or "male student", the pair of 女生. 生 means "student" here, as in 学生. 生 shows a shoot growing out of the ground, and means "to be born, to live".
column6: Wǒmen bān yǒu shí ge nánshēng.

column3: Girl or "female student". Use it for girls at school and for young women; for an adult woman in general the word is 女人.
column6: Nàge nǚshēng shì wǒ de tóngxué.

column3: Man, an adult male. Not the same as 男生, which is a boy or a male student. The pair is 女人.
Woman, an adult female, the pair of 男人. It is a plain description. To address someone, use 小姐 or 老师 or the name instead.
Boy. The 儿 turns the end of 孩 into an -r sound: nánháir. The same word without 儿, 男孩, is also used. 男 is 田 (field) over 力 (strength).
Girl, pronounced nǚháir. 孩 is 子 (child) with 亥 for sound. Add 小 for "little girl": 小女孩儿.
column6: Tā shì yī ge xiǎo nǚháir.

column3: Child, little kid, said xiǎoháir. Told to an adult it means "you are not a child": 你不是小孩儿了.
column7: You are not a little kid anymore.

column3: Elderly person: 老 (old) plus 人. 老 shows, on one reading, an old man with long hair leaning on a cane (耂 on top, 匕 below). Use it for people: 照顾老人 "look after the elderly".
column6: Zhè wèi lǎorén shì wǒ de yéye.
column7: This elderly man is my grandpa.

column3: Miss or "young lady", a title put after a surname: 王小姐 is Miss Wang. It is a fixed word, not "little older sister", and the second syllable is light: xiǎojie.
column6: Wáng xiǎojie shì wǒmen de lǎoshī.

column3: Mr. or "sir": 王先生 is Mr. Wang. Literally "born earlier" (先 plus 生). 先 is a foot 止 stepping in front of a person 儿 (to go forward). The 生 is light: xiānsheng.
Teacher, and also the way you address one, with or without a surname: 老师好！ 王老师. 老 ("old") shows respect here, and 师 means "master". The traditional form is 老師.
Classmate, fellow student. Teachers also use it to address students: 同学们好！ 同 means "same" and 学 means "study". The bottom of 学 is 子 (child) in both the simplified and traditional 學.
Doctor (the person): 王医生. To see a doctor is 看医生. In the traditional 醫 the bottom is 酉 (wine); it is the meaning part.
column7: I'm going to see the doctor tomorrow.

column3: Worker, a person doing manual or factory work: 工 plus 人. 工 is a picture of a tool (a spade or a carpenter's square).
Patient, sick person: 病 (illness) plus 人. In 病, 疒 (sickness) is the meaning part and 丙 the sound (bǐng, close to bìng).
column6: Yīyuàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō bìngrén.
column7: There are a lot of patients in the hospital.

column3: Online friend: a person you know only through the internet. 网 (net) plus 友 (friend). 网 is a picture of a net, and the traditional 網 adds 糹 (thread) with 罔 for sound.
Other people, someone else: 别人的书 "other people's books". Here 别 means "other"; before a verb it means "don't". On the right is 刂 (knife): 别 began as cutting bone from flesh, "to separate".
Year. Put it after the number: 三年 "three years", 二〇二五年 "the year 2025". It first meant "harvest" and later "year".
column6: Wǒ xué le liǎng nián Hànyǔ.
column7: I have studied Chinese for two years.

column3: Month and "moon": 三月 is March, 十二月 December, and 个月 counts months (两个月). It is a picture of a crescent moon. Elsewhere the same shape is not a moon: in 有 it is meat, in 朋 a string of shells.
Day and "sun". In dates the written form is 日 (三月五日) and speech says 号 (五号). It is a picture of the sun; the stroke in the middle was added to keep it apart from 口.
column4: 十月十三日是我的生日。
column5: 十月十三日是我的生日。
column6: Shíyuè shísān rì shì wǒ de shēngrì.

column3: The day of the month in speech: 五号 "the 5th". Also "number", as in a room or ticket number. 口 (mouth) with 丂, a mark for exhaled breath; the traditional 號 adds 虎 (tiger), from the idea of a roar.
Day and "sky": 今天, 三天, 天气. The old form was a standing person with the head stressed; the 一 over 大 is what is left of that.
column6: Yī tiān yǒu èrshísì ge xiǎoshí.

column3: Today, literally "this day". The word 今 means "now, this". Time words go before the verb: 今天我不忙.
Tomorrow. 明 is 日 (sun) beside 月 (moon): "bright". 明天见！ is a common way of parting.
Yesterday. In 昨, 日 (sun, day) is the meaning part and 乍 the sound, though zhà no longer sounds like zuó. Like other time words, it goes before the verb.
column7: I didn't go to school yesterday.

column3: The day after tomorrow. Here 后 is "after". In traditional writing the word is 後天: the traditional 后 is a different character, "ruler, sovereign". Taiwan writing uses 後 for "after, behind".
column7: The day after tomorrow is Saturday.

column3: The day before yesterday. 前 is "before, front". The 月 in it is not a moon: it is a worn-down 舟 (boat), since 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.
column7: The day before yesterday I was at home.

column3: This year. Year words go before the verb and need no 在: 今年我学汉语. The set is 去年, 今年, 明年.
Next year: 明 (bright) plus 年, in the same pattern as 明天. Place it before the verb: 明年我去中国.
column7: Next year I want to go to China.

column3: Last year. 去 elsewhere means "go", but here it means "gone by": 去 is the word for last year, not "go year".
column7: Last year I lived in Beijing.

column3: Week. Days are numbered: 星期一 Monday to 星期六 Saturday; Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日, never 星期七. In 星 the top 日 is a worn-down 晶 (a picture of stars); in 期 the 其 gives the sound.
column7: What day of the week is it?

column3: Sunday. The only day not named with a number; the same as 星期天. 日 means "sun, day".
column7: We don't have class on Sunday.

column3: Sunday, the same as 星期日, with 天 ("day") in place of 日. Ask which day with 星期几.
column7: Where do you want to go on Sunday?

column3: Birthday: 生 ("be born") plus 日 ("day"). 生日快乐 is "happy birthday". 生 shows a shoot growing out of the ground.
Date on a calendar: 日 (day) plus 期 (a fixed time). Ask 日期是几号？ 期 has 其 as its sound part (qí, close to qī).
Half a year. 半 comes before the measure word, but 年 and 天 need none, so 半年 and 半天; the others do take 个: 半个月, 半个小时.
column7: I studied Chinese for half a year.

column3: Half a day, and in speech "a long time": 我等了半天 "I waited ages". 半 needs no 个 here.
column7: I waited for you for ages.

column3: New Year: 新年好 or 新年快乐 as a greeting. In 新 the 斤 (axe) is on the right: it first meant "chop wood" (the original of 薪 "firewood") and was borrowed for "new".

Early, and "morning": 早 is also the greeting "morning!". 早 before a verb says early: 早睡 "go to bed early". It started as a picture of an acorn. As a way to remember (not history): the sun 日 just above the horizon.
column6: Nǐ jīntiān qǐ de zhēn zǎo.
column7: You got up really early today.

column3: Morning. Light 上: zǎoshang. Put the time before the verb and the clock time after: 早上七点. 早上好 is the greeting.
column7: I get up at seven in the morning.

column3: Morning up to noon: 上午九点. 午 means "noon" (a pestle, unrelated to 干); 上 here means "first half". The pair is 下午.
column7: I have class in the morning.

column3: Noon, midday: 中 (middle) plus 午 (noon). It is the usual time for lunch: 中午吃饭.
Afternoon: 下 plus 午. The word comes before the clock time: 下午三点, "3 p.m."
column7: I'm going to the shop this afternoon.

column3: Late and "evening": 太晚了 "too late". 日 (sun) is the meaning part and 免 the sound (miǎn, close to wǎn). Also in the set phrase 晚上好.
Evening, night: 今天晚上 is "tonight". Light 上: wǎnshang. 晚上好 is "good evening".
column7: I watch TV in the evening.

column3: Daytime, in contrast to 晚上: 白天上班，晚上休息. Literally "white day", meaning bright day.
Now: 现在几点？ It can come before or after the subject: 现在我很忙 or 我现在很忙. In 现, 王 (jade) is the meaning part and 见 gives the sound, close to xiàn.
Time, moment: 什么时候 asks "when". After a clause with 的 it means "when": 吃饭的时候. The 候 is light: shíhou.
Time as a stretch or amount: 有时间 "have time", 没时间 "have no time". For a clock time say 点: 三点. 间 means "between, space".
Hour as a length of time: 一个小时, 两个小时. A clock hour is 点, not 小时. 时 has 日 (sun) as meaning part; traditional 時 has 寺 as sound part where 时 has 寸.
column6: Wǒ xué le liǎng ge xiǎoshí.

column3: A little while, a moment: 等一会儿 "wait a moment". 会儿 is said huìr. 一会儿见 means "see you in a bit". Here 会 is not the verb "can".
Sometimes: 有 ("have") plus 时候 ("times"). It goes before the verb or at the start: 有时候我坐车. The short form is 有时.
Sometimes, the short form of 有时候. It is often paired for contrast: 有时…有时… ("sometimes… sometimes…").
column6: Wǒ yǒushí zuò chē, yǒushí zǒulù.
column7: I sometimes take a bus and sometimes walk.

column3: Right away, at once: 我马上来. Literally "on horseback": 马 ("horse") plus 上 ("on"). 马 is the simplified form of 馬, a horse with its mane.
column6: Nǐ děng yīxià, wǒ mǎshàng lái.
column7: Wait a moment, I'll be right there.

column3: O'clock: 三点, and 三点半 "half past three". Also "a bit" (一点儿) and "to order" (点菜). 占 gives the sound (zhàn); the meaning part is 灬 (fire) in 点 and 黑 (black) in the traditional 點.
Often: 常来 "come often". 巾 (cloth) is the meaning part and 尚 the sound. It first meant a lower garment (now written 裳) and was borrowed for "long-lasting; often".
column7: I often go to that shop.

column3: Often, the doubled form of 常: 他常常来. The usual negative is 不常, not 不常常. It goes before the verb.
column6: Tā chángcháng gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.

column3: First, beforehand: 先…再… means "first…, then…": 先吃饭，再看书. 先 is a foot 止 in front of a person 儿 (to go forward).
Again for something that has not happened yet: 再说一次 "say it once more". In 先…再… it means "then". For a repeat that already took place, Chinese uses 又 instead.
Last time: 上 ("previous") plus 次 ("occasion"). 上 itself is a short stroke above a long one. The next one is 下次.
column7: Where did you go last time?

column3: Next time: 下次再来 "come again next time". 下 mirrors 上: a short stroke under a long one.
Eat: 吃饭, 吃面包. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 乞 the sound, though qǐ no longer sounds like chī. 你吃了吗？ is a common greeting.
Drink: 喝水, 喝茶. Soup is also 喝, not 吃. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 曷 the sound.
column7: What do you want to drink?

column3: Cooked rice, and so "a meal": 吃饭 is "eat a meal". 饣 (food) is the meaning part and 反 the sound (fǎn, close to fàn); the traditional 飯 has 飠 for food.
Dish eaten with rice, and "vegetable": 点菜 is "order dishes". 艹 (plant) on top is the meaning part and 采 the sound (cǎi, close to cài).
Tea: 喝茶. 艹 (plant) is the meaning part on top. The modern 茶 comes from an older character for a bitter plant.
Water: 喝水, 热水. It is a picture of flowing water. At the left of other characters it becomes 氵 (河, 洗, 渴) and 水 also starts 水果.
Milk: 牛奶 is cow's milk. 女 (woman) is the meaning part and 乃 gives the sound, nǎi in both. 奶奶 "grandmother" uses it too.
Milk (cow's milk): 牛 plus 奶. 牛 is a picture of a bull's head with two horns and two ears. Drink it with 喝.
Cooked rice. 米 is raw rice (grains of rice) and 饭 is "meal". Rice that is still uncooked is just 米.
Bread: 面 ("flour") plus 包 ("wrapped thing"). In traditional writing the flour character is 麵 with 麥 (wheat) in it; the simplified 面 stands both for "face" and for 麵. So it is 麵包 in Taiwan.
column7: I eat bread in the morning.

column3: Noodles: 面 ("flour") plus 条 ("strip") plus the spoken ending 儿, giving miàntiáor. 条 is also the measure word for long thin things. Traditional 麵條兒 has 麥 (wheat) in the first character.
Steamed bun, usually with a filling: 肉包子. 包 means "wrap", so a 包子 is a wrapped thing; 包 is read as a baby 巳 inside a wrapping 勹. The 子 is light: bāozi.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng chī liǎng ge bāozi.
column7: I'd like to eat two buns.

column3: Meat: 吃肉, 牛肉. It is a picture of the ribs or a slice of meat. Inside other characters it shrinks to ⺼, as in 脑 (brain).
Egg, a chicken's egg: 鸡 ("chicken") plus 蛋 ("egg"). In 蛋, 虫 (insect, creature) is the meaning part; the traditional 雞 has 隹 (a short-tailed bird).
column6: Wǒ zǎofàn chī yī ge jīdàn.
column7: I eat an egg at breakfast.

column3: Fruit, as a food: 吃水果. Literally "water fruit". 果 is a picture of fruit growing on a tree (田 above 木). Name the fruit when you mean a particular one.
Tasty: 好 plus 吃, "good to eat". The same pattern works with other verbs: 好看 "good to look at", 好听 "good to hear", 好玩儿 "fun". The opposite is 难吃.
Eat a meal: a verb plus its object, so it can be split: 吃了饭 "have eaten". 你吃饭了吗？ asks whether someone has eaten.
Breakfast: 早 ("morning") plus 饭 ("meal"). The three meals are 早饭, 午饭, 晚饭.
Lunch: 午 ("noon") plus 饭. 午 is a picture of a pestle, and has nothing to do with 干.
Dinner, supper: 晚 ("evening") plus 饭. The verb is 吃: 吃晚饭.
Cup, glass. 杯 is the cup and 子 a light noun ending. 木 (tree, wood) is the meaning part of 杯 and 不 the sound, though bù only loosely matches bēi.
column7: There is water in the cup.

column3: Links a describing word or an owner to a noun: 我的书 "my book", 新的书 "a new book". It sounds like 得 and 地, which do other jobs: 地 comes before a verb (慢慢地走), 得 after a verb (走得快). Light tone: de.

A light particle for something done or new. After a verb: 我吃了饭. At the end of a sentence: 下雨了 "it has started to rain". It marks completion or change, not simply the past. The shape is a picture of a baby without arms.
column6: Wǒ chī le liǎng ge bāozi.

column3: A particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question: 你是学生吗？ Do not combine it with a question word like 什么 or 谁. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 马 (mǎ) the sound, nearly the same as ma.
column7: Do you have an older brother?

column3: A light particle for "and what about…?": 我很好，你呢？ Also asks where something is: 我的书呢？ After 在 or 正在 it adds a sense of "right now": 他在吃饭呢. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part.
A light particle that softens a suggestion or a request: 我们走吧 "let's go". Also asks for confirmation: 他是老师吧？ 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 巴 the sound, the same 巴 as in 爸.
A light particle after a verb that says a state continues: 门开着 "the door is open", 他坐着 "he is sitting". Taiwan writing uses 著; 着 is a variant of it with parts changed.

After a verb it says you have done it before: 我去过北京 "I have been to Beijing"; the negative is 没去过. As a verb it means "pass" or "spend": 过年. 辶 (walk) is the meaning part; the traditional 過 has 咼 where 过 has 寸.
A light particle that turns a describing word into an adverb before a verb: 慢慢地走 "walk slowly". Read dì it means "ground". Same sound as 的 and 得, so check the position: 地 comes just before the verb.
Right away, as early as, just: 我马上就来; 他八点就来了 "he came already at eight". It goes before the verb. The old form meant "go to a high place" (a tower), which has nothing to do with this use.
column6: Tā bā diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
column7: He was already up at eight.

column3: Still and "also": 他还在家 "he is still at home"; 还有 "there is also". 还 is also read huán "give back". 辶 (walk) is the part on the left in both 还 and the traditional 還.
Just (now), in the middle of doing something: 他正看书呢. Also "upright, correct": 正好 "just right". 止 (foot) is the lower part.
In the middle of doing: 我正在吃饭 "I am eating". It goes before the verb and stresses "right now"; 在 alone can mark this too, and 呢 at the end gives a spoken feel.
Don't before a verb: 别说话 "don't talk". Also "other" in 别人 and 别的. 刂 (knife) is on the right: it began as cutting bone from flesh, "to separate".
Some (of them): 有的人 "some people". Often paired: 有的…，有的… "some…, others…". The 的 is light: yǒude.
Come, toward the speaker: 他来了. Before a verb it means "let me do it": 我来介绍一下. The traditional 來 began as a picture of a wheat plant and was borrowed for "come".
Go, away from the speaker. A place follows directly, with no 到: 去学校, 去北京. There are several ideas for the shape and none is settled.
Return, go back: 回家, 回学校. It is a spiral, "turning around". With a direction it gives 回来 and 回去.
column7: What time do you go home?

column3: Arrive, reach: 到北京, 到家. After a verb it says the goal was reached: 看到, 找到. 至 ("arrive") is the meaning part and 刂 a form of 刀 giving the sound.
Enter: 进门; 进来 "come in", 进去 "go in". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part. The simplified 进 has 井 where the traditional 進 has 隹 (a bird).
Go out, come out: 出门, 出来, 出去. It is a foot 止 stepping out of a pit 凵; the modern shape no longer shows the foot.
Walk, "go", "leave": 我走了 "I'm off". It does not mean "run"; that is 跑. It is a running person (the top was once a different shape), with 止 (foot) added below.
Run: 跑得很快 "run fast". 走 is "walk" and 跑 only "run". 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 包 the sound (bāo against pǎo).
column7: The child is running on the road.

column3: Sit, and "travel by": 坐车, 坐飞机 "take a bus, a plane". 土 (earth, ground) is its lower part.
column7: I go to Beijing by train.

column3: Stand, and "station, stop": 车站. 立 ("stand") is the meaning part and 占 the sound (zhàn), the same 占 as in 点 and 店.
column7: He is standing at the door.

column3: Arrive at, come to: 来到北京 "come to Beijing". A place follows directly. It is 来 plus 到, "come and arrive".
Come back, toward the speaker: 他回来了 "he's back". The 来 is light and marks direction: huílai. The opposite is 回去.
Go back, away from the speaker: 我要回去了 "I have to go back". The 去 is light: huíqu. The opposite is 回来.
column6: Tài wǎn le, wǒ yào huíqu le.
column7: It's late, I have to go back.

column3: Go home: 回 plus 家, a verb and object, so no 到 or 去 is needed: 我回家. 家 means "home, family".
Return to: 回到家 "get back home". 到 says the place was reached; a place follows.
Come in, toward the speaker: 请进来. The 来 marks direction.
column7: Please come in and sit down.

column3: Go in, away from the speaker: 我们进去吧. The 去 marks direction.
Come out: 他出来了. After a verb it can mean "work out, make out": 看出来 "see that".
column7: He came out of the house.

column3: Go out: 我出去一下 "I'll step out". The 去 marks a direction away from the speaker.
column7: I'm going out to buy things.

column3: Sit down. 下 after a verb often marks downward movement: 坐下. The 下 is light: zuòxia.
Walk, on foot: a verb and its object, 走 ("walk") plus 路 ("road"). 走路去学校 is "walk to school".
Rise, get up: 起床, 起来; and in 一起 "together". 走 (walk) is the meaning part. The right part is one of the look-alikes 己 or 巳, so learn it by copying.
Get up, stand up: 请起来. After a verb or adjective it means "begin to": 笑起来 "start laughing". The 来 is light: qǐlai.
The general measure word: 一个人, 三个朋友, 两个杯子. When you do not know a noun's measure word, 个 is the safe choice. 个 is half of 竹 (bamboo); the traditional 個 has 亻 (person).
The measure word for books and notebooks: 一本书, 两本课本. It is 木 (tree) with an extra stroke at the bottom marking the roots, so "root". The stroke is what tells 本 from 木.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū.

column3: Cup and "cupful": 一杯茶 "a cup of tea". 木 (tree, wood) is the meaning part and 不 the sound part. 杯子 is the cup itself.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi shuǐ.
column7: Please give me a glass of water.

column3: The measure word for times something happens: 一次, 两次, 第一次. It is a person breathing out. Its right part 欠 is also in 歌 and 欢.
column6: Wǒ qù guo liǎng cì Běijīng.
column7: I have been to Beijing twice.

column3: Bag, "wrap", "pack": 书包 "schoolbag", 钱包 "wallet", 包子 "bun". It is a baby 巳 inside a wrapping 勹.
column6: Wǒ de bāo zài zhuōzi shang.
column7: My bag is on the table.

column3: The measure word for pieces ("一块肉") and, in speech, for money: 三块钱 "three yuan". 土 (earth) is the meaning part; traditional 塊 means a clod of earth, with 鬼 for sound where 块 has 夬.
Yuan, the written unit of money: 十元. In speech people usually say 块: 十块. It is a person with two lines stressing the head.
In speech, a tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is 0.5 yuan. The order of units is 块, 毛, 分. Also "hair, fur"; It is a picture of a feather or hair.
Minute: 三点十分 "ten past three". Also the smallest coin and a point in a score: 九十分. It is 八 ("to divide") over 刀 (knife), separating with a knife.
Money: 多少钱？ "how much?", 有钱 "rich". 钅 is the metal part, which also stands for money, and 戋 gives the sound; the traditional 錢 has 釒 and 戔.
column7: He has a lot of money.

column3: Wallet, purse: 钱 ("money") plus 包 ("bag").
Years of age, after the number: 二十岁. 你几岁？ is how you ask a child. the mountain-like top of 岁 is unrelated to 山; the traditional 歲 is built differently.
column7: My son is three years old.

column3: Some, a few: 一些人, 一些书, with no measure word. 些 is the plural measure also seen in 这些 and 那些. For a small amount of something uncountable, 一点儿 is used.
column7: There are some books on the table.

column3: A little, a bit: 一点儿水 "a little water". After an adjective it asks for "a bit more": 快一点儿 "a bit faster". The spoken ending 儿 makes it yīdiǎnr. Without 儿, 一点 can also mean "one o'clock".
column7: Please speak a little more slowly.

column3: Put after a verb to make it short and casual: 看一下儿 "take a look", 等一下儿 "wait a moment". 下 here counts one try or one action. The ending 儿 is spoken: yīxiàr. Also written 一下.
Some: 有些人 "some people". Before an adjective it means "somewhat": 有些累 "a bit tired". Compare 有的, used when others are set against the ones named.
There are some: 有一些人. It is 有 plus 一些, and 一些 takes no measure word before its noun. The same 些 appears in 这些 and 那些.
Few, little: 人很少 "few people". As a verb it means "do less": 少吃 "eat less". It is four dots meaning "a few", borrowing the sound of 小 (three dots).

Many, much: 很多人. A bare 多 before a noun sounds off, so say 很多 or 好多. Before an adjective it asks "how": 多大 "how big, how old", 多远 "how far". It is two pieces of meat, with the 夕 shapes worn down from 肉.
Together, the same as 一起: 我们一块儿去 "let's go together". 块 is also "piece" and "yuan", but here the word is said yīkuàir.
Half of something: 吃了一半 "ate half". It is a noun, so it takes no measure word. For a length of time, 半 comes in front: 半年.
Home, family: 我家有四口人. Also the measure word for shops and companies: 一家商店, 一家饭店. 宀 (roof) is the top; what is now written 豕 (pig) below was once a sound part.
At home: 在 plus 家. 他在家 means "he is home". Going home is a different word: 回家. 在家里 means the same.
At home, in the house or family: 家里有四口人. In traditional writing 家裡, because the "inside" 里 becomes 裡.
column7: There are a lot of books at home.

column3: House, flat: 买房子 "buy a house". 房 has 户 (door) as meaning part and 方 as sound part (fāng, close to fáng). The 子 is light: fángzi. For a room inside, the word is 房间.
Room: 我的房间. Not the whole house, which is 房子. 间 means "space between". A house has several: 三个房间.
column6: Wǒ de fángjiān zài èr lóu.
column7: My room is on the second floor.

column3: Restroom, toilet, literally "wash-hand room": 洗 plus 手 plus 间. Ask for it with 请问，洗手间在哪儿？
A measure word for rooms: 一间房; also "space between": 房间, 时间, 中间. The traditional 間 is a gate 門 with 日 inside; it is a variant of 閒, which had 月 (moon) there.
column6: Zhè ge fángzi yǒu sān jiān fáng.

column3: Door, gate: 开门, 关门. It is a picture of a gate. It frames the middle of many characters: 问, 们, 间, 开.
Doorway, entrance: at the door or just outside it. 口 ("mouth") also means "opening", as in 路口 "crossing".
column6: Xuéxiào ménkǒu yǒu yī ge shāngdiàn.
column7: There is a shop at the school entrance.

column3: Bed: 一张床; 在床上 "in bed". 广 (a house roof shape) plus 木 (wood): it is read as a wooden piece of furniture in a house.
Get up, out of bed: 起 ("rise") plus 床 ("bed"). A verb and its object, so 起了床 splits it.
Table, desk: 一张桌子; 桌子上 "on the table". 木 (wood) is the meaning part of 桌. The 子 is light: zhuōzi.
column7: The book is on the table.

column3: Building of several floors, and "floor": 二楼 is the second floor. 木 (wood) is the meaning part and 娄 gives the sound; both are lóu. The traditional 樓 has 婁.
column7: My home is on the third floor.

column3: Upstairs: the floor above. 楼上有人 "someone is upstairs". The pair is 楼下.
Downstairs: the floor below, or the ground outside the building: 在楼下等你.
Live, reside and "stay": 住在北京, 住三天. 亻 (person) is the meaning part and 主 gives the sound; both are zhù.
On, above, up. After a noun: 桌子上 "on the table". As a verb: 上班, 上课, 上车 ("go to, get on"). It is a short stroke above a long one; 下 is the reverse.
column7: Class is starting, please sit down.

column3: Below, down, and "get off, finish": 下车, 下班, 下课; also "fall" for rain: 下雨. It is a short stroke below a long one. After a verb 一下 softens it.
Inside: 家里, 书包里. In traditional writing that word is 裡 (clothing part 衤 with 里 giving the sound), while 里 itself is a unit of length: it is read as a field 田 on earth 土.
column7: The book is in the schoolbag.

column3: Outside, foreign: 门外, 外国, 外语. As a place word it follows the noun: 门外 "outside the door". The opposite is 里.
column7: There is someone outside the door.

column3: In front, before, ago. After a noun: 门前. After a time: 三年前 "three years ago". The 月 in it is a worn-down 舟 (boat), not the moon.
column6: Sān nián qián wǒ zhù zài Běijīng.
column7: Three years ago I lived in Beijing.

column3: Behind, after: 门后, 三年后 "in three years". Taiwan writing uses 後. 後 has a step 彳 and a foot 夂 held back by a thread 幺, "lagging behind".
column6: Sān nián hòu wǒ èrshí suì.
column7: In three years I will be twenty.

column3: Left: 左边. It began as a picture of a left hand, and 工 (work) was added underneath later. 右 is the same with 口 instead: 左 ends in 工, 右 in 口.
Right: 右边. It began as 又, a right hand and the same sound yòu, and 口 was added as a mark with no meaning. 右 ends in 口, 左 in 工.
East: 东边. 东 is the simplified form of 東; 東 began as a bag tied at both ends, and the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 is a later reading. 东西 means "thing".
column6: Wǒ jiā zài xuéxiào de dōngbian.
column7: My home is east of the school.

column3: West: 西边. Possibly a bird's nest, tied to the bird settling at sunset. 东西 is "thing" (and the East and West).
column7: The shop is west of the school.

column3: South: 南边. It was borrowed for its sound; the old shape was a lidded vessel.
column7: His home is south of the school.

column3: North: 北边, 北京 "northern capital". It is two people back to back; the word first meant "back", and "north" came from that.
column7: The school is north of the shop.

column3: Middle, center, and in 中国 "China". It is a flagpole, drawn as a vertical line through a box.
column7: He studies at a middle school.

column3: Beside, next to: 在…旁边. 我旁边 "beside me". 边 means "side".
Middle, between: 两个人中间 "between two people". 中 plus 间 ("space").
column6: Shūdiàn zài liǎng ge shāngdiàn zhōngjiān.
column7: The bookshop is between two shops.

column3: Above, on top, the upper side. Like the other place words in 边, the 边 is light: shàngbian.
column7: Your name is at the top.

column3: Below, underneath: 桌子下边 "under the table". Light 边: xiàbian.
column7: The book is under the table.

column3: Inside: 房间里边 "inside the room". In traditional characters 裡邊. Light 边: lǐbian.
Outside: 外边很冷 "it is cold outside". Light 边: wàibian.
In front, ahead: 前边有一家商店 "there is a shop ahead". Light 边: qiánbian.
column7: There is a shop up ahead.

column3: Behind, at the back. Traditional 後邊. Light 边: hòubian.
On the left: 左边 is "the left side". Light 边: zuǒbian. The pair is 右边.
column7: My home is to the left of the school.

column3: On the right. Light 边: yòubian. Used with 坐在 to say where someone sits.
column7: The teacher sits on my right.

column3: East side. Light 边: dōngbian. Chinese lists compass points as 东南西北 ("east, south, west, north").
column7: There is a train station on the east side.

column3: West side. This dictionary gives 西边 a full first tone on 边: xībiān. The compass order in Chinese is 东南西北, so west comes third.
column7: To the west there are mountains.

column3: South side: 南边. Light 边: nánbian. 南 is the second of 东南西北.
column7: My home is in the south.

column3: North side. This dictionary gives 北边 a full first tone on 边: běibiān. 北 is last in 东南西北.
column6: Xuéxiào běibiān yǒu yī jiā shūdiàn.
column7: North of the school there is a bookshop.

column3: Used twice, for two actions at once: 一边…一边… "while…ing, …ing". Put one before each verb.
column6: Tā yībiān zǒulù yībiān tīng gē.
column7: He listens to songs while he walks.

column3: Look, watch, read: 看书, 看电视, 看电影; 看病 "see a doctor". It is a hand 手 over an eye 目, shading the eyes to see far.
Listen, hear: 听歌, 听说 "I hear that". The simplified 听 is unrelated to the traditional 聽, which contains 耳 (ear).
Speak, say: 说汉语, 说话. 讠 (speech) is the meaning part and 兑 the sound, though duì no longer sounds like shuō. The traditional 說 has 言.
Read aloud, study: 读课文 "read the text aloud"; 读书 "study, go to school". 讠 (speech) is a left part; traditional 讀 has 言.
column6: Qǐng dú yīxià zhè ge zì.

column3: Write: 写字, 写汉字. It always takes an object or a result: 写错了. The traditional form is 寫.
Ask: name the person first: 问老师 "ask the teacher". 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 门 (mén) the sound, close to wèn.
column6: Tā wèn wǒ jiào shénme míngzi.
column7: He asked me what my name is.

column3: Answer, a verb and a noun: 回答问题 "answer a question"; 他的回答 "his answer". 回 ("return") plus 答 ("reply").
Be called: 我叫王明; or "call, tell to": 叫他来 "have him come". 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 丩 the sound. 你叫什么名字？ is the standard question.
column6: Wǒ jiào Wáng Míng, nǐ jiào shénme?
column7: My name is Wang Ming, what's yours?

column3: Name: 你叫什么名字？ In 名, one explanation is 夕 (evening) over 口 (mouth): saying your name to be known in the dark. In 字, 子 gives the sound. The 字 is light: míngzi.
Tell: 告诉我 "tell me". The person comes straight after it, without 对: 告诉他, not 告诉对他. 诉 has 讠 (speech) as meaning part. The 诉 is light: gàosu.
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de míngzi.

column3: See, catch sight of: 看 plus 到, where 到 says the seeing worked. 我看到他了 "I saw him". Compare 看见.
column6: Wǒ kàndào nǐ de lǎoshī le.

column3: See, catch sight of, like 看到: 我看见他了. In 见, the traditional 見 is read as a kneeling person with a big eye for a head.
column6: Nǐ kànjiàn wǒ de qiánbāo le ma?

column3: Hear: 听 plus 到 says the sound reached you. 我听到了 "I heard it". Compare 听见. 听 alone is "listen", which is trying.
Hear, like 听到: 我听见有人叫我. The 见 ("see, perceive") after the verb says the sound reached you, as 看见 says the sight did. 听 alone is only "listen".
Speak, talk: a verb and its object, so it can split: 说了很多话 "talked a lot". 话 means "words, speech". 说 and 话 both have the speech radical, 讠 (traditional 言).
Study, go to school: 他在北京读书 "he studies in Beijing". It can also mean "read a book". 读 plus 书, "read" plus "book".
Dictation: 听 ("listen") plus 写 ("write"). The teacher reads out words and students write them down. Used as: 有听写, 做听写.
Smile, laugh: 笑了. With a person, "laugh at": 笑他. On top is ⺮ (bamboo) and below 夭 as the sound part; the oldest form had 艸 and 犬 instead.
Sing: 唱一首歌 "sing a song". 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 昌 the sound.
column6: Nǐ huì chàng zhè shǒu gē ma?

column3: Sing: a verb and its object, so it can split: 唱了一首歌. In 歌, 欠 is the meaning part and 哥 gives the sound, gē in both.
See and "meet", seldom alone: 看见, 听见, 再见, 见面, 见到. The traditional 見 is read as a kneeling person with a big eye for a head; the simplified 见 comes from handwriting.
Meet, see each other: a verb and its object, so no object follows it. Say 跟朋友见面 "meet a friend", not 见面朋友.
Introduce, explain: 介绍朋友 "introduce a friend"; 自我介绍 "introduce yourself". In 绍, 纟 (thread) is the meaning part and 召 the sound; the traditional 紹 has 糹.
column4: 我来介绍一下，这是我的朋友。
column5: 我來介紹一下，這是我的朋友。
column6: Wǒ lái jièshào yīxià, zhè shì wǒ de péngyou.
column7: Let me introduce you, this is my friend.

column3: Speech, words: 说话, 电话, 一句话 "a sentence". 讠 (speech) is the meaning part. In the traditional 話, the right part only looks like 舌 (tongue): it is a different component.
Study, learn: 学汉语. 子 (child) is the bottom part of both 学 and the traditional 學. 學 is read as hands and a roof over 爻, with the child added later.
Student, a pupil of any level: 学 plus 生. For a fellow student you also hear 同学.
column6: Wǒmen bān yǒu èrshí ge xuésheng.

column3: Study, learn: 学习汉语. Both verb and noun: 他的学习很好. 习 was cut down from 習, which is read as wings 羽 over the sun 日 (later 白), "learning to fly by practice".
column7: He is studying in the library.

column3: School (the place and institution): 我的学校. 校 has 木 (wood) as meaning part and 交 as sound part.
College, institute, a school inside or beside a university: 医学院 "medical school". 院 has 完 as sound part (wán, close to yuàn).
column7: He studies at the medical school.

column3: University, college: 上大学 "go to university". 大 ("big") plus 学.
column7: He goes to university in Beijing.

column3: University student: 大学 plus 生 ("student").
column7: My older sister is a university student.

column3: Primary school: 上小学. 小 ("small") plus 学. Next comes 中学 and then 大学.
column7: My younger brother is in primary school.

column3: Primary-school pupil: 小学 plus 生 ("student"). The ending 生 also works in 中学生 and 大学生, so the whole ladder is built the same way.
Secondary school, lower and upper together: 中 ("middle") plus 学.
column7: I teach Chinese at a secondary school.

column3: Secondary-school student: 中学 plus 生. It covers pupils from the first year of lower secondary school to the last of upper secondary school.
Go to school, attend school: 上 ("go to") plus 学. About school in general, not one class; for a class, 上课.
column7: My younger brother goes to school at eight.

column3: School is out: 放 ("let go") plus 学. 放学后 means "after school".
column6: Fàngxué hòu wǒmen qù wánr ba.

column3: Teaching building of a school or university: 教学 ("teaching") plus 楼 ("building"). 教 is read jiào here, not jiāo.
column7: We have class in the teaching building.

column3: Teach: teacher, then person, then subject: 她教我汉语. 攵 (a hand with a stick) and 子 (child): teaching a child. Read jiāo as a verb; jiào in 教学楼.
Have class, go to class, teach a class: 上课了 "class has begun". 课 has 讠 (speech) as meaning part and 果 (guǒ) as sound part, though kè no longer sounds like guǒ. 上学 is school in general.
Class is over: 下课了. The opposite of 上课. 下 here means "finish".
column7: Class is over, let's go eat.

column3: Class, lesson: 第三课 "lesson 3", 一节课 "one class period". 讠 (speech) is the meaning part; traditional 課 has 言.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu sān jié kè.

column3: Textbook: 课 ("lesson") plus 本 ("book"). 请打开课本 is a teacher's usual instruction.
Text of a lesson, the passage in a textbook: 读课文. In 文 the shape is read as a man with a tattooed chest; today it means "writing, text".
Book: 一本书, 看书, 买书. The simplified 书 comes from cursive writing of 書, which has a writing brush 聿 at the top.
Schoolbag, book bag: 书 ("book") plus 包 ("bag"). 包 is also in 钱包 "wallet", and in 包子 where it means "wrap". Carry one: 背书包.
Notebook: 本 ("book, volume") plus the light ending 子, běnzi. Count with 个 or 本: 两个本子.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng ge běnzi.

column3: Character, written word: 汉字, 写字, 一个字. 宀 (roof) is the meaning part and 子 the sound (zǐ against zì).
column7: How do you read this character?

column3: Chinese characters: 汉 plus 字. 汉 is "Han"; 漢 is named after the Han river, and 氵 is water. 写汉字 is what this app practices.
column7: I am learning to write Chinese characters.

column3: Chinese, the language: 学汉语, 说汉语. The HSK is the 汉语水平考试, "Chinese language level test". 语 has 讠 (speech) as meaning part and 吾 as sound part.
Chinese as a language, especially in writing: 学中文, 中文书 "Chinese books". 中 ("China") plus 文 ("writing").
Foreign language: 外 ("foreign") plus 语 ("language"). 学外语 "study a foreign language".
column7: What foreign language do you want to learn?

column3: Take a test: 考汉语 "take a Chinese test". 考 is a variant of 老: both show an old person leaning on a cane, which is why they share 耂.
column7: We have a Chinese test tomorrow.

column3: Exam, test, and "to take an exam": 明天有考试; 考试了吗？ 试 has 讠 (speech) as meaning part and 式 as sound part, both shì.
Try: 试一下 "give it a try"; 试穿 "try on". 讠 (speech) is the meaning part and 式 the sound, both shì; the traditional 試 has 言.
Page: 第三页 "page 3". 頁 first meant a person's head, and was later used for "page", through 葉 ("leaf, page").
Class, a group of students who learn together: 我们班. Not a lesson, which is 课. It is a knife 刂 cutting between two pieces of jade 王.
Want to: 我想去. Also "miss": 我想你; and "think": 想一想. Gentler than 要. 心 (heart) is the meaning part and 相 the sound, which differs from xiǎng only in tone.
Want, need, will: 我要一杯茶; 我要走了 "I'm about to go". Stronger than 想. 不要 means "don't", not just "don't want". It is a woman 女 under a drawing of hands at the waist, which became 覀.
column7: I'll have a cup of tea.

column3: Can, for something learned: 我会说汉语. Also "will": 明天会下雨; and "meeting": 开会. The traditional form is 會.
Can, when circumstances or permission allow: 我今天不能去. Where 会 is a learned skill, 能 is ability or possibility. It is a bear, with two 匕 for paws; later borrowed for "can".
Like: 喜欢茶, 喜欢吃. 很喜欢 is "like a lot". The second syllable is light: xǐhuan. 喜 is read as a drum 壴 over a mouth 口; 欢 has 欠 (breath) as meaning part.
Love: 我爱你. Stronger than 喜欢. Also "love to do": 他爱吃肉. The simplified 爱 replaces the bottom of 愛 with 友 (friend); 愛 has 心 (heart) in the middle.
Hobby: 你的爱好是什么？ Here 好 is read hào, "to like", not hǎo. 爱 ("love") plus 好 ("be fond of").
Good-looking, and "worth watching or reading": 好看的电影. The same pattern as 好吃 and 好听. The opposite is 难看.
column7: This piece of clothing looks nice.

column3: Pleasant to hear: 好听的歌. 好 plus 听, "good to listen to". The opposite is 难听.
Happy, glad: 很高兴认识你 "nice to meet you". 兴 is read xìng here, not xīng. The traditional 興 is read as four hands lifting an object.
column7: I'm very glad to meet you.

column3: Get angry: 别生气 "don't be angry"; 生他的气 "be angry with him". Literally "produce breath": 生 plus 气 ("air, spirit"). A verb and its object, so 生了气 splits it.
Feel, think: 我觉得很好 "I think it's good". A soft way to give an opinion. 觉 is read jué here; in 睡觉 it is jiào. 觉 has 见 (see) as meaning part.
column6: Wǒ juéde zhè ge hěn hǎo.
column7: I think this one is good.

column3: Do, make: 做饭 "cook", 做什么 "do what". It is a later variant of 作 with the same meaning; the two sound the same, zuò. 亻 (person) is the left part.
Do, work at (gàn), in speech: 干什么, 这件事我来干. In traditional writing this gàn is 幹, which has 干 inside it. The other 干 (gān, "dry") is 乾 there. 干 is a shield.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ lái gàn.

column3: Buy: 买东西 "go shopping". The opposite, 卖 (mài, "sell"), looks almost the same and sounds the same but for the tone, so check which one you mean. In the traditional 買, the top 罒 is a net, not an eye, and 貝 is a shell (money).
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī běn shū.
column7: I want to buy a book.

column3: Thing, stuff: 买东西 "go shopping", 好东西 "good stuff". With a light xi, dōngxi. Read dōngxī with full tone, it means "east and west".
Take, hold: 拿书 "hold a book"; 拿来 "bring". 手 (hand) is the lower part.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ ná yīxià shū.
column7: Please hold the book for me.

column3: Put, place: 放在桌子上 "put it on the table". Also "let go": 放学, 放假. 攵 (action, a hand with a stick) is the meaning part and 方 the sound; fàng and fāng differ by tone.
Give (as a gift), "see off", "deliver": 送你一本书; 送朋友 "see a friend off". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part.
column6: Wǒ sòng nǐ yī běn shū.

column3: Use: 用手机 "use a phone"; 用中文说 "say it in Chinese". 不用 means "no need".
Useful: 有 plus 用, "have use". The pattern 有 plus a noun makes an adjective: 有用, 有名. The opposite is 没用.
Get, obtain: 得到帮助 "get help". 得 is read dé in this word; the light particle 得 is de. The old form is a hand grabbing a cowry shell, with 彳 (step) added.
column6: Tā dédào le yī běn shū.

column3: Give back, return: 还书 "return books", 还钱 "pay back". The same character is also hái "still". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part.
Hit, and the verb for many actions: 打球, 打电话, 打车. Which verb goes with which noun is learned phrase by phrase. 扌 (hand) is the meaning part and 丁 the sound.
Open, "turn on", "drive", "hold (a meeting)": 开门, 开车, 开会. The traditional 開 is read as a gate 門 with two hands lifting the latch; the 开 part is those hands and latch merged.
Close, "turn off": 关门, 关电视. The traditional 關 shows the gate 門; the simplified 关 drops it.
Close, with the result that it is shut: 关上门 "shut the door". The 上 after the verb says the closing is done. The opposite is 打开.
Open, with the result that it is open: 打开门 "open the door", 打开书 "open the book". 打 plus 开, "strike open". Also for turning something on: 打开电视. The opposite is 关上.
Move: 别动 "don't move". Mostly found inside longer words. 力 (strength) is the meaning part; the traditional 動 has 重 (zhòng) as sound part, close to dòng, where 动 has 云.
Movement, action: a physical motion, in exercise, dance or gesture. 动作很快 "quick movements". 动 ("move") plus 作 ("make").
Big. Also "old" for people's age: 你多大了？ It is a person facing forward, arms out. 太 is 大 with a dot added, so don't add one by accident.
Small, little: 小房间. Also a friendly prefix before a surname: 小王 for a younger person. It is three dots, perhaps grains of sand.
column6: Zhè ge bēizi tài xiǎo le.

column3: Tall, high: 他很高. It is a picture of a tall building. For comparison, 他比我高 "he is taller than me".
New, before a noun: 新书, 新房子. Opposite of 旧. On the right is 斤 (axe): the character first meant "chop wood" and was borrowed for "new".
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī ge xīn bēizi.

column3: Old, for people or long-standing things: 老朋友 "old friend". For objects that are not new, 旧 is used instead. It is an old man with long hair leaning on a cane.
column6: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou.

column3: Bad, broken: 电脑坏了 "the computer is broken"; 坏人 "a bad person". 土 (earth) is the meaning part; the traditional 壞 has 褱 where 坏 has 不. The earth part is there because what rots goes back to earth.
Fast: 快走 "hurry". Also "soon": 快八点了 "it's almost eight". 忄 (heart) is the meaning part and 夬 the sound, the same 夬 as in 块.
Slow: 慢走 is a goodbye to someone leaving, "take care". 忄 (heart) is the meaning part and 曼 the sound; both are màn.
column6: Nǐ zǒu de tài màn le.

column3: Difficult: 难写 "hard to write". 难 plus a verb works like 好 plus a verb: 难吃 "bad to eat". Traditional 難 has 隹 (a bird) as the meaning part. Read nàn it means "disaster".
column7: Chinese characters are hard to write.

column3: Expensive: 太贵了. Also polite "your" in 您贵姓？ "what is your surname?". 贝 (shell, once used as money) is the lower part; traditional 貴 has 貝.
White and "bright": 白天 "daytime". There are two theories, an acorn or a human head. 百 is 白 with 一 on top, bǎi against bái.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì bái de.
column7: This piece of clothing is white.

column3: Heavy: 书包很重. Read zhòng as in 重要. It is a person carrying a bag, with 土 added to stand for the ground.
Dry (gān): 衣服干了 "the clothes are dry". In traditional writing "dry" is 乾; the other 干 (gàn, "do") is 幹. 干杯 "cheers" means "dry the cup".
Clean: 房间很干净. 洗干净 "wash clean". Here 干 is gān and 净 jìng. Traditional 淨 has 氵 (water) as the meaning part.
Poor, lacking: 他的汉语很差. For time, "short of": 差五分三点 "five to three". Read chā it means "difference".
column6: Xiànzài chà wǔ fēn sān diǎn.

column3: Far: 学校很远; 离…远 "far from…". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part and 元 the sound, close to yuǎn. The traditional 遠 has 袁.
column6: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn yuǎn.
column7: My home is far from school.

column3: Famous: 有 ("have") plus 名 ("name"). 有名的人 "a famous person". Same pattern as 有用.
Important: 很重要. 重 ("heavy") plus 要 ("essential"). 重 is read zhòng here, not chóng.
Serious, conscientious: 认真学习 "study conscientiously". 认 ("recognize") plus 真 ("real"). In 认, 讠 (speech) is the meaning part and 人 the sound, differing only in tone: rèn and rén.
Body and "health": 身体好 "healthy", 身体不好 "not well". 身 began as a picture of a pregnant woman. In the traditional 體, 骨 (bone) is the meaning part.
On one's body, on one's person: 身上没有钱 "I have no money on me". Light 上: shēnshang.
column7: I have no money on me.

column3: Hand: 洗手; 手机. It is a hand with the fingers splayed. At the left of characters it becomes 扌, as in 打, 拿 and 找.
Mouth, and the measure word for family members: 四口人. Also "opening": 门口, 路口. It is an open mouth. Keep it apart from 日 (sun), which has a stroke inside.
column6: Tā jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
column7: There are three people in his family.

column3: Illness: 他的病好了 "his illness has gone". Also "to be ill": 他病了. 疒 (sickness) is the meaning part and 丙 the sound (bǐng, close to bìng).
column7: He has recovered from his illness.

column3: See a doctor (as a patient), and "treat a patient" (as a doctor): 去医院看病. 看 here means "to examine".
column7: I'm going to the hospital to see a doctor tomorrow.

column3: Fall ill: 他生病了. 生 here means "come about", as in 生气: 生 plus 病. A verb and its object.
Tired: 我很累, and for tiring work: 工作很累. The reading with a field and silk is a folk etymology; the simplified 累 is a shortening of 纍.
Sleep: 睡一会儿 "have a nap". 目 (eye) is the meaning part and 垂 the sound, chuí against shuì.
Sleep, go to bed: a verb and its object, so 睡了一觉 "had a sleep". 觉 is read jiào here, not jué.
column7: I go to bed at ten.

column3: Hungry: 我饿了 "I'm hungry". 饣 (food) is the meaning part and 我 the sound, though wǒ is far from è now. The traditional 餓 has 飠.
column6: Wǒ è le, wǒmen chīfàn ba.

column3: Thirsty: 我渴了. 氵 (water) is the meaning part and 曷 the sound. 又饿又渴 is "both hungry and thirsty".
column6: Wǒ hěn kě, xiǎng hē shuǐ.
column7: I'm very thirsty, I want some water.

column3: Electricity and "lightning", mostly the start of other words: 电话, 电脑, 电视, 电影. The traditional 電 has 雨 (rain) on top, for the storm.
column7: The power is out at home.

column3: Phone, phone call: 打电话 "make a call"; 电话号码 "phone number". 电 ("electric") plus 话 ("speech").
column6: Nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshao?

column3: Computer: 电 ("electric") plus 脑 ("brain"). 脑 has ⺼ (flesh) as its meaning part. 开电脑 "turn on the computer".
Television: 看电视. 视 has 见 (see) as meaning part and, in the traditional 視, 示 as sound part, which is also shì.
Television set, the machine: 买电视机. 机 has 木 (wood) as meaning part and 几 as sound part, jī against jǐ. 看电视 is "watch TV".
Movie, film: 看电影; 电影院 "cinema". 影 first meant "shadow"; 彡 is the meaning part and 景 the sound.
column7: Do you want to watch a movie?

column3: Mobile phone: 手 ("hand") plus 机 ("machine"). 用手机 "use a phone". 手机号 is a mobile number.
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī zài zhuōzi shang.
column7: My phone is on the table.

column3: Make a phone call: 打 plus 电话. The person called goes before the verb: 给他打电话 "call him".
Go online: 上 ("get on") plus 网 ("net"). A verb and its object: 上了网. 上网看新闻 "read the news online".
column7: I go online in the evening.

column3: Online, on the internet: 网上买东西 "shop online". As a place word, it follows 在 and comes before the verb.
Song: 一首歌; 唱歌. 欠 is the meaning part and 哥 gives the sound, gē in both.
Play, have fun, hang out: 去哪儿玩儿. 玩 has 王 (jade) as meaning part and 元 as sound part (yuán against wán). The spoken ending makes it wánr.
Fun, interesting to play with: 好 plus 玩儿, like 好吃 and 好看. 这里很好玩儿 "this is a fun place".
Joke, kid around: 开 ("make") plus 玩笑 ("joke"). 别开玩笑 means "you're kidding".
Ball and "ball game": 一个球; 打球. 王 (jade) is the meaning part and 求 the sound, qiú in both; it first named a kind of jade.
Play ball games: 打 plus 球. 打球 is for games like basketball or tennis; football is 踢球, "kick the ball".
column7: We play ball in the afternoon.

column3: Country: 中国, 国家. In the simplified 国, 玉 (jade, treasure) sits inside the border 囗; the traditional 國 has 或 there.
Country, nation: 国 plus 家. 每个国家 "every country". Used for the state; for a country's people, 人: 中国人.
column6: Nǐ qù guo jǐ ge guójiā?
column7: How many countries have you been to?

column3: Abroad: 去国外 "go abroad". A place, not a describing word: 国外 is abroad, 外国 is foreign (外国人).
Foreign country, before a noun "foreign": 外国朋友, 外国人. Compare 国外 "abroad", which is a place.
column6: Wǒ yǒu hěn duō wàiguó péngyou.

column3: China: 中 ("middle") plus 国 ("country"). 中国人 is a Chinese person. 中 is also read zhòng in other words.
Beijing: 北 ("north") plus 京 ("capital"). 京 is a picture of a tall building. A proper name, so the pinyin is capitalized.
Shop, store: 去商店; 一家商店. 店 has 广 (a building) as meaning part and 占 (zhàn) as sound part, the same 占 as in 点 and 站.
column7: What time does the shop close?

column3: Shopping mall, big store. 场 means "open space": 土 (earth) is the meaning part. A 商店 is a shop; a 商场 is a large one with many.
column7: We're going to the mall to buy clothes.

column3: Hospital: 医 plus 院. 去医院 "go to the hospital"; 看病 is what you do there. 院 has 完 as sound part (wán, close to yuàn).
Cinema: 电影 plus 院 ("hall, institution"). 在电影院看电影 "watch a movie at the cinema".
Ground, land: 地上 "on the ground"; 地方 "place". 土 (earth) is the meaning part and 也 the sound. The light particle de (慢慢地走) is a different job for the same character.
column7: There is water on the ground.

column3: Place: 好地方 "nice place", 什么地方 "what place". 方 is light: dìfang.
Location, venue: 时间和地点 "time and place". 点 here means "point".
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ shíjiān hé dìdiǎn.
column7: Please tell me the time and place.

column3: On the ground, on the floor: 书在地上. Light 上: dìshang.
column7: The book is on the floor.

column3: Map: 一张地图; 看地图. 图 is "picture"; the traditional 圖 is read as a territory 啚 inside a boundary 囗, which suits a map.
Restaurant or "hotel", depending on the name and the place: 北京饭店. 饭 ("meal") plus 店 ("shop").
column6: Zhè ge fàndiàn de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is delicious.

column3: Bookshop: 书 plus 店. 在书店买书 "buy books at the bookshop".
column7: The bookshop is next to the school.

column3: Library: 图 ("picture") plus 书 plus 馆 ("hall"). 馆 has 饣 (food) as meaning part and 官 (guān) as sound part, and names buildings for public use.
Vehicle: car, bus, bicycle: 坐车, 开车, 车站. It is a picture of a two-wheeled cart seen from above; the simplified 车 is from cursive writing of 車.
Car: 开汽车, 坐汽车. 汽 has 氵 (water) as meaning part and 气 as sound part (qì in both); it is read as water in the form of air, steam. 汽车 is literally "steam vehicle".
Train: 火 ("fire") plus 车 ("vehicle"). 坐火车; 火车站. 火 is a picture of flames, written 灬 at the bottom of characters.
column7: What time does the train arrive?

column3: Airplane: 飞 ("fly") plus 机 ("machine"). 坐飞机 "go by plane". 飛 is a bird flying upward, and 飞 is its shortened form.
Fly: 飞机, 飞到北京. It is a picture of a bird in flight; the traditional 飛 is the longer form of the same picture.
Station, stop: 火车站, 汽车站. 车 plus 站, "vehicle standing place". 站 has 立 (stand) as meaning part and 占 as sound part.
column7: There are a lot of people at the station.

column3: On the vehicle, in the car: 车上有很多人 "the bus is crowded". Light 上: chēshang.
column7: My book is in the car.

column3: Ticket for a bus or train: 买车票. 车 plus 票. The measure word is 张: 一张车票.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng chēpiào.

column3: Airport: 机 ("plane") plus 场 ("open ground"). 去机场; 机场很大.
column7: I'm waiting for you at the airport.

column3: Plane ticket: 机 ("plane") plus 票 ("ticket"). 买机票 "buy a plane ticket"; the measure word is 张: 一张机票. Compare 车票 for a bus or train.
column7: The plane ticket is too expensive.

column3: Ticket: 车票, 机票, 门票. Count with 张: 一张票. The lower 示 replaced an earlier 火 (fire); the word first meant sparks rising and then "token" or "ticket".
Admission ticket, for a park, museum or show: 门 ("door") plus 票. 买门票.
column7: An admission ticket is twenty yuan.

column3: Get on a bus, train or car: 上 plus 车. 请上车. The opposite is 下车.
Get off a bus, train or car: 下 plus 车. 在哪儿下车？ asks where. The opposite is 上车.
Road, way: 马路, 走路; also a bus route: 三路车. 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 各 the sound (gè against lù).
Intersection, crossing: 路 plus 口 ("opening"). 在路口等 "wait at the intersection".
On the way, on the road: 路上小心 "be careful on the way", said to someone setting off. Light 上: lùshang.
Road, street with traffic: 马 ("horse") plus 路. 过马路 "cross the street".
Drive: 开 plus 车. A verb and its object: 开了一个小时的车. 你会开车吗？ Compare 打车, which is to hail a taxi.
Take a taxi, hailing or calling one: 打 plus 车. Not 开车, which is driving yourself.
Clothes: 一件衣服; 穿衣服. 衣 is a picture of a garment's upper part. In 服 the 月 is not a moon: it is a worn-down tray or boat shape. The 服 is light: yīfu.
column7: This piece of clothing is expensive.

column3: Wear clothes and shoes: 穿衣服, 穿白衣服. It is 穴 (cave) over 牙 (tooth), meaning "go through". For a hat or glasses a different verb is used.
Wash: 洗手, 洗衣服. 氵 (water) is the meaning part and 先 the sound (xiān against xǐ).
column7: I'm going to wash my hands.

column3: Weather: 天 ("sky") plus 气 ("air"). 天气好 "good weather"; ask 天气怎么样？
Rain: 大雨 "heavy rain". It is a cloud with drops falling. 雨 is at the top of 零 and 电.
Rain: 下 ("fall") plus 雨. No subject is needed: 下雨了 "it has started to rain".
Wind: 大风 "strong wind"; 有风. The traditional 風 started as a drawing of a phoenix, borrowed only for its sound.
Mountain: 山上 "on the mountain". It is three peaks. Don't mix it with 出, whose top is not a mountain.
Tree: 一棵树. 木 (tree) is the meaning part; the simplified 树 has 对 as its second part where the traditional 樹 has 尌.
column6: Shān shang yǒu hěn duō shù.
column7: There are many trees on the mountain.

column3: Flower, and "to spend": 花钱 "spend money". 艹 (plant) is the meaning part and 化 the sound, huà against huā.
Hot: 天气很热; 热水. Also "popular", as in 热闹. 灬 (fire) is the meaning part. The opposite is 冷.
Cold: 天气很冷. 冫 (ice) is the meaning part and 令 the sound, close to lěng; the same 令 is in 零.
Go to work, be at work: 上 plus 班 ("shift"). A verb and its object. For a class, say 上课.
Finish work, leave work: 下 plus 班. 下班后 "after work". The opposite is 上班.
column7: What time do you finish work?

column3: Work: a job (找工作) or a verb (在北京工作). 工 is a picture of a tool and 作 means "do".
Have a meeting: 开 ("hold") plus 会 ("meeting"). A verb and its object: 开了一个会.
column7: We have a meeting in the afternoon.

column3: Matter, affair: 什么事 "what's the matter"; 有事 "have something on". It is a hand holding a flag, as in "doing one's job".
column7: What can I do for you?

column3: No problem, it's nothing, also "I'm free". A reply to an apology: 没事儿，不用谢. The ending 儿 is spoken: méishìr.
column7: No problem, no need to thank me.

column3: Busy: 我很忙. 忄 (heart) is the meaning part and 亡 the sound. 忘 has the same 亡 and looks alike, but with 心 underneath: 忙 máng, 忘 wàng.
Prepare, get ready: 准备早饭; 准备 plus a verb is "plan to". Traditional 準備. 備 is read as a person 亻 carrying a quiver, "ready".
Rest, take a break: 休息一下. 休 is a person 亻 leaning against a tree 木; 息 is a nose 自 over a heart 心, "to breathe". The 息 is light: xiūxi.
Have time off, a holiday for school or work: 放 ("release") plus 假. 假 is read jià here. For one person's leave, 请假.
column7: We have a day off tomorrow.

column3: Ask for leave: 请 ("ask for") plus 假 ("leave"). A verb and its object: 请了一天假 "took a day off". Compare 放假, when everyone is off.
column7: I need to ask for leave tomorrow.

column3: Help: 帮我买 "buy it for me". The helped person comes first, then the action: 帮 plus person plus verb. The simplified 帮 has 邦; the traditional 幫 has 封.
Help, do a favor: a verb and its object, so no object follows it. Say 帮我的忙 or 帮他一个忙, not 帮忙我. 谢谢你帮忙 is "thank you for helping".
Know a fact: 我知道; 我不知道. For people and places use 认识 instead. 知 has 口 (mouth) as meaning part and 矢 as sound part.
column6: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā de míngzi.

column3: Know a person, "recognize" a character: 我认识他; 认识这个字. For a fact, use 知道. Light 识: rènshi. In 认, 人 gives the sound, differing in tone (rèn, rén).
column6: Nǐ rènshi zhè ge zì ma?

column3: Remember, "note down": 记得, 记住, 记笔记. 讠 (speech) is the meaning part and 己 the sound, jǐ against jì. 己 is easy to mix with 巳 and 已, so copy the shape carefully.
column6: Wǒ jì bu zhù zhè ge zì.

column3: Remember (still have in mind): 我记得他的名字. The opposite is 忘记 or 忘了. Light 得: jìde.
Memorize, remember firmly: 记住这个字. 住 after a verb says the thing stays put. Negative: 记不住 "can't hold it in mind".
Forget: usually with 了: 我忘了 "I forgot". 心 (heart) is the meaning part and 亡 the sound, wáng against wàng. 忙 has the same 亡, but 忄 at the left.
column6: Wǒ wàng le nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ.

column3: Forget: 忘记 plus an object: 忘记了他的名字; 别忘记 "don't forget". Same meaning as 忘, with 记 added.
column7: Don't forget to close the door.

column3: Understand: 我明白了 "I get it". 明 ("bright") plus 白 ("clear"). The 白 is light: míngbai.
Knowledge: 有知识 "knowledgeable". 知 ("know") plus 识 ("recognize"). 识 has 讠 (speech) as meaning part and 只 as sound part. The 识 is light: zhīshi.
column6: Shū lǐ yǒu hěn duō zhīshi.
column7: There is a lot of knowledge in books.

column3: Wait: 等我 "wait for me" takes the person directly, no 对. ⺮ (bamboo) is the meaning part; it stood for bamboo strips used to sort writing. 寺 gives the sound.
Look for: 找朋友, 找工作. The popular story of a hand 扌 looking for a halberd 戈 is a mnemonic, not the character's origin. 找到 is "find".
column6: Wǒ zài zhǎo wǒ de shǒujī.

column3: Find, having looked: 找到 plus the thing. The negative splits it: 找不到 "can't find".
column6: Wǒ zhǎodào wǒ de qiánbāo le.

column3: And, "with": 我和你 "you and I". It joins nouns, not sentences or verbs. 禾 (hé) gives the sound and 口 is the meaning part, "harmony".
column6: Wǒ hé wǒ mèimei shì tóngxué.
column7: My younger sister and I are classmates.

column3: With, "and", "follow": 跟我来 "follow me"; 跟朋友一起去; 跟…一样 "the same as". 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 艮 the sound, gēn in both.
From: 从北京来 "come from Beijing"; 从…到… "from … to …". The character is two 人 (people), one following the other.
column6: Wǒ cóng bā diǎn xué dào shí diǎn.
column7: I study from eight to ten.

column3: Than, for comparing: A 比 B plus an adjective, 他比我高. After 比 do not add 很: not 他比我很高. It is two spoons 匕 side by side.
Give, "for": 给我 "give me"; 给他打电话 "call him". 纟 (thread) is the meaning part and 合 the sound, though hé is far from gěi; the traditional 給 has 糹.
column6: Wǒ gěi māma mǎi le huā.

column3: Together: 我们一起去. It goes before the verb. The same as 一块儿.
The same: A 跟 B 一样, 我的书跟你的一样. Add an adjective for "as … as": 跟他一样高. 样 has 木 (tree) as meaning part and 羊 as sound part; the traditional 樣 has 羕.
column6: Wǒ de shū gēn nǐ de yīyàng.
column7: My book is the same as yours.

column3: Finally, last: 最后一个 "the last one". 最 ("most") plus 后 ("after"). Traditional 最後.
column7: In the end we all went home.

column3: Or, in questions: 你喝茶还是喝水？ A statement uses 或者 instead. Also "had better, still prefer": 还是你去吧. Traditional 還是.
column6: Nǐ hē chá háishi hē shuǐ?
column7: Do you want tea or water?

column3: Also, there is also: 还有一本书. As a question, 还有吗？ means "anything else?".
Most: 最大, 最好, 最喜欢. It goes before an adjective or verb. It is also the first part of 最后 and 最好.
Best, and "had better": 你最好休息 "you'd better rest". 最 plus 好.
column7: You had better go to bed early.

column3: Other, else: 别的人 "other people", 别的东西 "something else". Light 的: biéde. 别 here is "other", not "don't".
column6: Nǐ hái yǒu biéde shì ma?
column7: Do you have anything else on?
